factors.verdict: tiny difference, but it is a lexical artifact, not extraction quality: the offline MetaSchemaExtractor stores the numeric value in structured.schema.fields, and store.search_text flattens every structured field into the BM25 text, so 6 vs 12 changes the index. field_completeness is 1.0 at both levels and the fact set is unchanged.

real but small and ranking-only: lambda=0.001 wins by +0.0136 nDCG vs 0.01 and +0.0119 vs 0.05; 0.01 is the low point, so the curve is non-monotone with a shallow dip. Recall, tokens and redundancy are unchanged because decay only reorders the same 15 candidates. Low decay roughly preserves the incoming order; stronger decay reorders by recency.

only 500 bites: 340.4 vs 344.6 tokens (-1.2%) with recall/nDCG unchanged; 1000 and 2000 are identical to the 4000 default because the 15-unit context is only ~345 tokens. There is no quality/token tradeoff to tune at 1000/2000; 500 is a mild token-only saving.

R4 k is now live: 10/15/25 change mean candidates 8.47/12.79/21.45, Recall@15 0.4206/0.4619/0.4913, nDCG 0.2638/0.2746/0.2700, tokens 227.4/344.6/578.9. k=25 buys +0.029 recall at -0.0045 nDCG and +234 tokens; k=10 saves 117 tokens at -0.041 recall. This is a real budget tradeoff, not a flat curve.

MMR lambda is live once decay is off: nDCG 0.3268 (0.5) / 0.3282 (0.7) / 0.3292 (0.9); recall, tokens and redundancy are unchanged because MMR only reorders. λ=0.9 is best by +0.0024 nDCG vs 0.5 (95% cluster CI [+0.0010, +0.0042], excludes 0). This is a small ranking-only effect. MMR×decay stage-order interaction is NOT tested; decay was fixed off.

max_neighbors is now wired (GraphIndex.expand caps neighbours per frontier node; default None keeps old behaviour), but the 10/40/80 scan is still identical: graph_khop is used on only 23/240 questions and the 15-candidate budget is filled by other channels, so the cap is not binding. This is a query-routing/budget result, not evidence that the parameter is unread.
